title: Night Truth Burned
warm:
Night-truth burned meant [player_name] watched the gap she could have spoken become ash—mercy or cowardice, Crownspire would not decide for her. Early thirties, she/her, across-the-hall neighbor—she stood with Nolan Greer in the penthouse hush while paper curled and Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rose downstairs without a body. Vivienne's four fates stayed open: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging.

"You burned what you saw," Nolan said, mid-forties holding, brutal charm, cufflinks clicking once then still. "Soft alibi keeps its throat. Soft also means Brooks may invent a sharper version if yours stays ash." Wind sheer. Elevator chime. Unused perfume from the master bath she should not know. Marcus Pell would call it traveling management. Rhea Quinn's slate still held thinning marks.

[player_name] did not invent a corpse by burning testimony. She did not invent Milan. Ash only proved she had chosen silence over naming—and that Vivienne's cadence could still be method or coincidence depending on which fear she fed. Soft meant pliable evidence that might now be reconstructed against her.

Across the hall, colder sheets. Black car at the curb. Wine rings like complicity. Hope and dread shared the smoke.

"Blow Crownspire open anyway," Nolan murmured, "or let the handler escape while I hunt and you wait across the hall. Neither settles Vivienne. Both spend the burn."

She catalogued mercy versus cowardice the way Brooks would: ash, no settled body, soft still claimed. Crownspire held its hush. [player_name] felt the burned night-truth watching her mouth, and understood that ash had already changed which soft she could still swear.
hot:
Night-truth burned as heat under smoke—[player_name] felt Nolan Greer's hands on her waist while ash cooled and want refused to. Early thirties, across-the-hall aching, mid-forties money pressed close enough that cufflink metal kissed her hip. Vivienne's perfume haunted every inhale as third heat. Soft alibi had a pulse; burning the gap made the pulse filthy with unfinished questions.

"You chose ash," he murmured against her ear. Rain-money cologne. Brooks's homicide interest vibrated through glass without a corpse. Crime stayed plot; sex stayed intimacy-forward. Four fates open; her cunt clenched around mercy and cowardice like twin verbs.

His thumb counted ribs. "Open Crownspire's silence—or wait across the hall while I hunt the handler who escapes. Both leave you wet. Neither boxes my wife."

She arched, thighs tight, perfume-haunted. Mid-want ending first—climax belonging to the next choice. His hips brushed; the almost ached louder than smoke.

"If I open it," she whispered, "I spend ash into public heat with your hands still on me." A beat. "If I wait across the hall, I keep private throb and unfinished chase."

Elevator chime trembled through her teeth. Wind sheer. Wine-ringed marble. Black car curb-idle. She trembled choosing, unfinished on purpose, romance locked on Nolan Greer alone while Vivienne stayed contested.
